0Executive summary

Overall risk: CRITICAL. The production network configuration trusts user-installed CAs, bundles a Charles Proxy CA, permits cleartext, and enforces no certificate pinning. Together this makes full traffic interception (including Authorization: Bearer tokens) trivial for an on-path attacker or a malicious profile.

Mrsool is a large on-demand delivery & services super-app: ordering, courier mode, chat (XMPP), payments (Paymob / OPPWA 3-D Secure), subscriptions (“Mrsool Black”), groceries, stickers, and an AI concierge (“Butler”). It is built with Kotlin + Jetpack Compose, 8 DEX files, ~41.5k classes, and ships native libraries for device fingerprinting and credential crypto.

Key findings
  • Critical — MITM-ready TLS profile: base-config trusts user CAs and permits cleartext for every domain; manifest sets usesCleartextTraffic=true; no pinning.
  • Critical — Charles Proxy CA (mrsool_ca.pem) bundled and trusted in production.
  • High — device-fingerprint & anti-tamper stack (Bureau) with recoverable obfuscated keys.
  • Medium — broad exported surface + mrsool:// / App-Links deep links.
  • Medium — expired own root CA (mrsool_root_ca.pem, expired 2025-07-12).

4Architecture & package map

Multi-package Kotlin + Compose super-app with MVVM/MVP mixed architecture, Room, Retrofit/OkHttp, Apollo GraphQL, XMPP (Smack) and a Bureau native fingerprinting stack.

Secret derivation (decompiled)

void Java_com_mrsool_utils_Secrets_getProductionApiKey(JNIEnv *env, jclass, jstring s) {
    const char *p = GetStringUTFChars(env, s, 0);
    char hex[65]; sha256(p, hex);
    for (i = 0; i < 32; i++)
        out[i] = hex[i % strlen(hex)] ^ embedded_table[i];
    return NewStringUTF(env, out);
}
Keys are not plaintext: they are SHA256(passphrase) XOR static table. Since both inputs live in the app, every “protected” key is recoverable at runtime with Frida/instrumentation. This is obfuscation, not cryptographic protection.

Integrity checks

Root detection (checkForRoot) and Frida/hook detection (checkFrida, isPathReallyExist) are native, string/`/proc`-based and bypassable with standard Frida scripts.

11TLS / cleartext audit

<network-security-config>
  <debug-overrides><trust-anchors>

  </trust-anchors></debug-overrides>
  <base-config cleartextTrafficPermitted="true">
    <trust-anchors>
      <certificates src="@raw/mrsool_ca"/>
      <certificates src="@raw/mrsool_root_ca"/>
      <certificates src="user"/>
      <certificates src="system"/>
    </trust-anchors>
  </base-config>
</network-security-config>
PropertyResult
Cleartext defaultEnabled for all domains
Trusts user-installed CAsYes — in base-config (production)
Bundled CA #1Charles Proxy CA — CN=Charles Proxy CA (28 Mar 2020, Suaads-MacBook-Pro.local), O=XK72 Ltd, 2000-01-01 → 2049-05-24, SHA-256 1E99BF36…4671
Bundled CA #2Own root O=Mrsool, CN=Mrsool.co, self-signed, 2023-04-09 → 2025-07-12 (expired)
Other bundled CAscomodo_ca.crt, sectigo_ca.crt (not referenced by NSC)
Certificate pinningNone (only OkHttp library class; no pins)
Impact: an attacker on the network path, or anyone who can install a CA profile, can decrypt and modify all app traffic, steal bearer tokens, session cookies, chat messages and PII.

12Security findings

SeverityFindingImpact / remediation
CriticalUser-CA trust in production base-configFull TLS interception. Remove <code>src="user"</code>; use system trust + pinning.
CriticalCleartext traffic permitted for all domainsDowngrade/MITM. Set <code>cleartextTrafficPermitted=false</code>; remove manifest flag.
CriticalCharles Proxy CA bundled and trustedDebug proxy CA in release. Remove <code>res/raw/mrsool_ca.pem</code> and reference.
HighNo certificate pinningAdd SPKI pinning for api/ws/xmpp hosts.
HighObfuscation-only secret storageKeys recoverable via instrumentation. Scope/rotate keys; server-side secrets.
MediumBroad exported surface + deep linksValidate all intent extras; protect sensitive activities with permissions.
MediumExpired own root CA trustedRemove expired anchor.
MediumRoot/Frida detection bypassableDo not rely on it for security decisions.
InfoallowBackup=falseGood.

13Reconstruction blueprint (agent-ready)

13.1 Recommended stack

  • Language/UI: Kotlin, Jetpack Compose + Material 3; Navigation Compose.
  • Architecture: MVVM, feature modules (auth, home, order, chat, payment, me, butler).
  • Networking: Retrofit + OkHttp (REST v6), Apollo Kotlin (GraphQL), OkHttp WebSocket (ActionCable), Smack (XMPP chat).
  • Local: Room, DataStore, WorkManager.
  • Maps/location: Google Maps + FusedLocation; Huawei Map Kit fallback.
  • Media: Coil/Glide, Lottie, ExoPlayer/Media3.
  • Push: FCM + Huawei Push Kit.
  • Payments: Paymob Accept SDK + OPPWA 3-DS2.
  • Analytics/observability: Firebase, Sentry, Amplitude, CleverTap, Intercom.
  • Fraud: Bureau device intelligence.

13.2 Module structure

app/
 ├─ core/ network, auth, session, di, ui-kit, analytics
 ├─ feature-auth/        phone/OTP, Nafath, Absher, Facebook, face verification
 ├─ feature-home/        feed, services, stores, search (Algolia + REST v6)
 ├─ feature-order/       create order, cart, checkout, reorder, order details
 ├─ feature-chat/        XMPP + REST conversations, butler AI, media, bills
 ├─ feature-payment/     cards, Paymob, OPPWA 3-DS2, wallet, subscriptions
 ├─ feature-courier/     courier mode, assignments, shift management, heatmap
 ├─ feature-me/          profile, addresses, settings, delete account
 ├─ feature-support/     Intercom help center, tickets, surveys
 ├─ feature-stickers/    WhatsApp-style sticker packs (content provider)
 └─ feature-grocery/     grocery catalog / search / cart

13.3 Core flows to implement

  1. Auth: phone → OTP (auth/signin / users/{{userid}}/verify_code), Nafath/Absher for Saudi IDs, Facebook login, face verification WebView.
  2. Home/search: REST v6 + Algolia indexes; carousels/surveys via content/*.
  3. Order: store/menu → cart → business_orders/submit/validate → payment → live tracking via WebSocket.
  4. Chat: XMPP connect to xmpp.mrsool.co; REST fallback (conversations/*, api/v1/chat*).
  5. Payment: payins/payin_options → payins/payin_transactions → 3-DS via OPPWA/Paymob → poll check_status.
  6. Courier mode: accept/assign, live location (location/*), shift schedule, order state transitions (orders/{{order_id}}/update_order_state).
  7. Subscriptions: “Mrsool Black” options, manage, cancel.

13.4 Backend contract checklist

Implement the REST endpoints in §6.3 (121 app endpoints across tq.d, tq.a, tq.g, tq.f, tq.e, hp.a), the GraphQL endpoint, the ActionCable WebSocket and XMPP. All requests carry Authorization: Bearer and device_id; GraphQL requests carry Apollo operation headers.

V2-0UI & resource inventory overview

This volume documents everything needed to reproduce the user interface, copy and local data layer of Mrsool: design tokens, every layout, every string, menus, navigation, fonts, drawables, manifest specifics, preferences and assets. Class names, API contracts and backend behaviour are in Volume I.

Layout files896 across 9 configuration folders
Colors1256
Dimensions1139
Strings3064 (default locale) · plurals 54 · string-arrays 11
Styles / themes1510 defined · 227 referenced by layouts
Drawables2593 unique (animated-vector: 27, animation-list: 6, bitmap: 1084, inset: 1, layer-list: 20, ripple: 11, selector: 111, shape: 440, transition: 6, vector: 765, xml: 122)
Fonts11 font resources
Menus6 · navigation graphs 0
Animations88 anim XML · raw resources 78
Assets46 entries
Screen → layout mappings217 classes resolved
Local persistenceDataStore classes 2 · SharedPreferences holders 23 · Room databases 0
How to use this volume. Layout trees show the exact view hierarchy, ids, literal texts, sizes and orientations. Design values (colors/dimens/styles) are given in full, so a rebuilt layout will look identical. Exact attribute-level XML and binary assets are additionally shipped in the companion archive resources/mrsool_res.zip (see §V2-9).
No @Composable functions and no Room databases were found in the app code: the UI is classic Android Views + XML layouts (Material Components / AppCompat), and persistence uses DataStore/SharedPreferences plus the network cache. Any library-bundled Compose runtime is unused by app screens.
